heroIntro: A split-second act of reckless driving on a Bangladeshi highway or urban thoroughfare can instantly destroy a family's future. When a sole earning parent is killed or a child suffers permanent catastrophic injury, transport owners and syndicates routinely vanish, leaving grieving families crushed under funeral expenses and intensive care bills.

quickAnswer.title: Quick Answer: How to Claim Compensation for Road Accidents in Bangladesh
quickAnswer.text: Under the Road Transport Act 2018 and Road Transport Rules 2022, victims or their surviving heirs can claim statutory financial compensation from the government Financial Assistance Fund (Trustee Board): BDT 5,00,000 for fatal accidents, BDT 3,00,000 for permanent loss of limb, and up to BDT 1,00,000 for medical treatment. Concurrently, families can institute substantial civil tort lawsuits for crores of taka in damages against bus and truck owners under the Fatal Accidents Act 1855, and initiate non-bailable criminal prosecution under Section 105 of the Road Transport Act 2018.

sections.title: The Devastation of Road Accidents and Legal Rights in Bangladesh
sections.content:
Imagine your spouse, parent, or child setting off on a routine inter-district bus journey or daily commute in Dhaka, only for your family to receive a devastating phone call from a highway police outpost. A speeding long-haul bus or overloaded heavy truck operating without a valid fitness certificate lost control, resulting in a fatal collision. In an instant, the family's sole economic breadwinner is gone, leaving dependents overwhelmed by grief and looming financial catastrophe.

Historically in Bangladesh, victims of road crashes and their families were left entirely abandoned. Transport owners and powerful transport worker federations routinely protected reckless drivers, while insurance companies used cumbersome procedures to evade third-party liability claims under the outdated Motor Vehicles Ordinance 1983.

However, modern statutory enactments have transformed this legal terrain. With the operationalization of the Road Transport Act 2018 and the landmark compensation precedents established by the Supreme Court of Bangladesh, victims possess powerful, enforceable legal rights to demand immediate statutory financial relief, substantial tort damages, and stringent criminal accountability.

sections.title: Statutory Framework: Road Transport Act 2018 Overview
sections.content:
The enactment of the Road Transport Act 2018 (Act No. 47 of 2018) replaced the colonial-era Motor Vehicles Ordinance 1983, establishing a rigorous legal framework for road safety, vehicle fitness, driver accountability, and victim rehabilitation.

Crucially, the Act created two distinct legal mechanisms for accident victims:

  • Statutory Financial Assistance Fund (Section 53): An institutionalized, permanent compensation fund established under the Bangladesh Road Transport Authority (BRTA) to disburse immediate financial assistance to accident victims and their families without requiring lengthy courtroom trials.
  • Stringent Criminal Penalties (Sections 66, 84, 98, and 105): Substantially heightened criminal sanctions for reckless driving, driving without valid licenses, operating unfit vehicles, and causing death or grievous hurt.

By decoupling basic financial compensation from the outcome of criminal trials, the law ensures that impoverished families do not have to wait a decade for criminal convictions before receiving emergency financial aid.

sections.title: The Financial Assistance Fund: Statutory Compensation Rates
sections.content:
Under Section 53 of the Road Transport Act 2018, read with the Road Transport Rules 2022, the government established the Financial Assistance Fund (Aarthik Shohayota Tohobil), managed by an independent Board of Trustees headquartered at the BRTA.

The rules establish guaranteed statutory compensation ceilings for road accident casualties:

  • Fatal Accidents (Death): A mandatory lump-sum payment of BDT 5,00,000 (Five Lakh Taka) payable directly to the legal heirs and dependents of the deceased victim.
  • Permanent Disability or Loss of Limb: A lump-sum payment of BDT 3,00,000 (Three Lakh Taka) for victims suffering permanent paralysis, amputation of limbs, loss of eyesight, or traumatic brain injury.
  • Grievous Physical Injury: Up to BDT 1,00,000 (One Lakh Taka) for major surgical treatments, prolonged hospitalization, and medical rehabilitation.

These statutory payments are non-repayable grants funded through mandatory annual contributions paid by commercial motor vehicle owners during vehicle registration and fitness renewals.

sections.title: Step-by-Step Claim Procedure Before the Trustee Board
sections.content:
Securing compensation from the Financial Assistance Fund requires adhering to a strict administrative procedure established under the Road Transport Rules 2022:

  1. Strict 30-Day Limitation Window: Under Rule 151, the victim or their legal heirs must submit their formal compensation application to the Chairman of the Trustee Board (BRTA) within 30 days of the accident. If delayed due to medical hospitalization, an application for extension with medical certificates must be filed.
  2. Prescribed Application Form: The claim must be submitted on Form-39, specifying accident details, vehicle registration numbers, police station FIR numbers, hospital admission records, and applicant bank details.
  3. Inquiry by Inquiry Committee: The Trustee Board forwards the claim to a local inquiry committee comprising the Upazila Nirbahi Officer (UNO) or Executive Magistrate, the local police officer-in-charge (OC), and a government medical officer.
  4. Verification and Recommendation: The committee inspects the accident scene, verifies the police report, and submits an assessment report to the Trustee Board within 30 days.
  5. Disbursement via Bank Transfer: Upon approval, the Trustee Board issues an account-payee cheque or direct electronic fund transfer (BEFTN) to the victim or legal heirs within 30 days of receiving the inquiry report.

sections.title: Mandatory Documents & Evidence Gathering Checklist
sections.content:
A compensation claim will be summarily rejected if the supporting evidentiary portfolio is incomplete. Your legal team must systematically secure the following documents:

  • Police Documentation: A certified copy of the Thana FIR, General Diary (GD) entry, or Highway Police seizure list confirming the date, time, location, and involved vehicle registration numbers.
  • Medical Evidence: Original hospital discharge certificates, surgical notes, medication receipts, and a permanent disability certificate issued by a government Medical Board or Civil Surgeon.
  • Post-Mortem & Death Certificate: In fatal cases, the official autopsy report from a government medical college hospital and the municipal or Union Parishad death certificate.
  • Proof of Heirship: An authentic Succession Certificate from the civil court or Warishan Sanad (Heirship Certificate) issued by the local Ward Councilor or Union Parishad Chairman, accompanied by NID cards of all legal heirs.

sections.title: Civil Lawsuits for Substantial Tort Damages: Fatal Accidents Act
sections.content:
While BDT 5 Lakh from the BRTA Trust Fund provides immediate emergency assistance, it is utterly inadequate to compensate for the loss of a young parent or professional whose lifetime earnings would have exceeded crores of taka. Fortunately, claiming Trust Fund aid does not forfeit your right to pursue substantial civil damages.

Under the Fatal Accidents Act 1855 and common-law tort principles, surviving dependents can institute a comprehensive civil damage suit in the Joint District Judge Court against the transport company, the bus owner, and the driver. In the historic, precedent-setting judgment of Catherine Masud vs. Md. Kashed Miah and Others (2017), the High Court Division awarded over BDT 4.61 Crore in compensation to the family of renowned filmmaker Tareque Masud, establishing landmark legal rules:

  1. Strict Vicarious Liability: Transport companies are financially responsible for the negligent and reckless driving of their employed drivers.
  2. Calculation of Lifetime Loss: Courts calculate compensation based on the deceased's monthly income, future career promotions, dependency multiplier, and personal living expenditures.
  3. Joint and Several Decrees: Decrees can be executed directly against the bank accounts, commercial vehicle fleets, and immovable properties of the transport owners.

sections.title: Criminal Prosecution Against Reckless Drivers and Owners
sections.content:
Simultaneously with financial claims, criminal accountability must be pursued to prevent the offending driver and transport owner from escaping justice:

  • Section 105 Road Transport Act 2018: Any person causing death or grievous injury through reckless or negligent driving shall be punished with imprisonment of either description for a term which may extend to 5 years, or with a substantial fine, or with both. This offense is strictly non-bailable.
  • Section 98 RTA 2018 (Dangerous Driving): Penalizes speeding, dangerous overtaking, and driving in contravention of road signals with up to 3 years imprisonment.
  • Owner Liability (Sections 66 & 77): Vehicle owners who knowingly assign an unfit vehicle, an unlicensed driver, or permit overloaded passenger transit can be prosecuted as criminal co-accused.
  • Vehicle Seizure and Custody: The offending vehicle is impounded by the police under a formal seizure list (Jobdo-talika) and cannot be released without court permission, providing immense leverage during settlement negotiations.

sections.title: Illustrative Scenario: Securing Trust Fund and Civil Compensation
sections.content:
Illustrative scenario (composite; names and details changed): Mahbub, a 36-year-old marketing manager and father of two young children, was traveling from Cumilla to Dhaka on the highway when a reckless inter-district passenger bus, racing another vehicle, slammed head-on into his microbus. Mahbub was killed instantly, while two other passengers suffered severe spinal fractures. The bus driver fled the scene, but highway police impounded the bus.

Devastated and facing immediate mortgage and school fee defaults, Mahbub's widow consulted a specialized accident litigation advocate within two weeks of the tragedy. Her legal counsel took swift, synchronized action:

First, within 25 days of the crash, a complete Form-39 claim was submitted to the BRTA Financial Assistance Fund, accompanied by the police FIR, highway seizure list, post-mortem report, and heirship certificates. Within 75 days, the Trustee Board disbursed BDT 5,00,000 directly into the widow's bank account, providing essential immediate relief.

Second, her advocate filed a comprehensive civil tort lawsuit under the Fatal Accidents Act 1855 in the Joint District Judge Court, claiming BDT 1.85 Crore in loss of lifetime dependency against the bus company and its primary shareholders. Concurrently, criminal prosecution under Section 105 RTA 2018 prevented the transport company from retrieving the impounded BDT 90 Lakh luxury bus without securing significant court bail bonds, ultimately compelling the transport syndicate to settle the civil damage claim for BDT 75 Lakh.

faqs.q: What is the deadline to apply for financial assistance from the Road Transport Trust Fund?
faqs.a: Under Rule 151 of the Road Transport Rules 2022, the application for financial assistance must be submitted to the Chairman of the Trustee Board (BRTA) strictly within 30 days from the date of the road accident. If the victim was unconscious or hospitalized, an application for extension with certified medical records must be submitted.

faqs.q: Does receiving BDT 5 Lakh from the Trust Fund prevent the family from filing a civil damages lawsuit?
faqs.a: No. Statutory financial assistance received from the BRTA Trust Fund under Section 53 of the Road Transport Act 2018 is an emergency welfare grant and does not forfeit or extinguish the legal heirs' right to file a civil lawsuit for substantial tort compensation under the Fatal Accidents Act 1855.

faqs.q: What documents are strictly required to prove a road accident compensation claim?
faqs.a: The mandatory documents include: (1) Certified copy of the Thana FIR or General Diary (GD), (2) Police accident seizure list, (3) Post-mortem / autopsy report or medical board disability certificate, (4) Original medical bills and treatment vouchers, (5) Death certificate and Warishan Sanad (Heirship Certificate), and (6) National ID copies of legal heirs.

faqs.q: Can the family sue the bus or truck company directly if the driver fled the scene?
faqs.a: Yes. Under the doctrine of vicarious liability, the registered owner and transport company are legally liable for damages caused by vehicles operated under their commercial management. The family can file a civil suit for damages in the Joint District Judge Court against the registered owner regardless of whether the driver was arrested immediately.

faqs.q: How do courts calculate lifetime loss of earnings in a road accident tort suit?
faqs.a: Following the Supreme Court precedent in the Catherine Masud case, courts assess the victim's monthly income, calculate expected future promotions and career longevity up to retirement age (typically 60 to 65 years), deduct personal living expenses (typically one-third), and apply an actuarial dependency multiplier.

faqs.q: Can a passenger injured inside a public bus or ride-sharing car claim compensation?
faqs.a: Yes. Passengers injured while traveling inside buses, minibuses, ride-sharing vehicles, or auto-rickshaws have full legal standing to claim statutory medical compensation from the BRTA Trust Fund and sue both the transport operator and the other colliding vehicle for civil damages.

faqs.q: What criminal charges can be brought against a driver who drove without a valid driving license?
faqs.a: Under Section 66 of the Road Transport Act 2018, driving without a valid professional license is punishable with imprisonment for up to 6 months, or fine up to BDT 25,000, or both. If reckless driving without a license results in death, the driver faces prosecution under Section 105, carrying up to 5 years non-bailable imprisonment.

faqs.q: How can a family obtain a certified copy of the police accident report (FIR and Charge Sheet)?
faqs.a: The family or their engaged advocate can apply directly to the Officer-in-Charge (OC) of the concerned Thana or Highway Police Outpost, or submit a formal court application to the Chief Judicial or Metropolitan Magistrate Court where the police station records are submitted.
